lxc_bf545b659ed95ff9.text: Newest AI research for robotics is moving from chatbots toward models that see, plan, and act.

lxc_945499cae3c01bf7.text: Real systems like JEPA, V-JEPA 2, and Vision-Language-Action models help explain the change, and a simple robot-arm example shows what robots actually use today.

lxc_c2f4531b43a41b7d.text: For the last few years, most people met AI through chatbots.

lxc_09e24b3b0447da92.text: You type a question, and a large language model, or LLM, writes an answer.

lxc_a4a95e8c276980dc.text: But words are only one part of the world.

lxc_3a6c55c2da75fa53.text: Newest AI research for robotics points in a clearer direction.

lxc_9043f4522b056649.text: Models need to see, plan, and act.

lxc_e9696b5ea26bdec4.text: Seeing means using images and video, not only text.

lxc_219bac7763751bba.text: Planning means predicting what will probably happen next.

lxc_2f4864209a61f0d8.text: Acting means controlling something real, like a robot arm.

lxc_43f6790abf2729fa.text: People often use three words for this direction.

lxc_e8727526d2e2b66a.text: Multimodal means many kinds of input.

lxc_e55fb9588645fc9d.text: Agents means models that take steps toward a goal.

lxc_3a5e716780ae4677.text: World models means models that learn how the physical world usually behaves.

lxc_98511614953ae691.text: Keep this simple lens in mind.

lxc_607bef63fdcdaea9.text: We will use it in every part below.

lxc_67d069c98f191ea0.text: Imagine you tell a robot in a Japanese kitchen, "Put the rice bowl on the tray."

lxc_f53be42e4a19055c.text: A text LLM can read that sentence perfectly.

lxc_8bc903e289b306cd.text: But it has no eyes, so it does not know where the bowl is.

lxc_0af286cc68be248b.text: It has no hands, so it cannot move anything.

lxc_e9ce18fd840d7bf6.text: And it has no sense of timing, so it does not know how fast to close the fingers before the bowl slides.

lxc_55a855d10ab639e3.text: A robot needs vision to find the bowl and see if it is full or empty.

lxc_b1f0cc1ae85be474.text: It needs actions, which are small commands like "move the arm 2 centimeters left" or "close the gripper."

lxc_041b5b0de572e7db.text: And it needs timing, because the real world does not wait.

lxc_534970c6a75fd836.text: If the arm moves too late, the bowl is already falling.

lxc_a6083acd707d11bb.text: It tells the robot the goal.

lxc_723fc3fe41da7ce0.text: But the goal is only the start.

lxc_2ec577e454c5c921.text: The see-plan-act loop must run many times every second.

lxc_1eb027c31c17626d.text: The first big answer to this gap is the Vision-Language-Action model, or VLA.

lxc_fc41e463e3cea315.text: A VLA takes an image from the robot's camera and a text instruction, and it gives out robot actions directly.

lxc_65da0078f5cc71c6.text: Vision, language, and action are joined in one model.

lxc_50ac4a966ce78217.text: Two real projects show how this works.

lxc_c73233b8eeb3ea9b.text: Open X-Embodiment is a shared dataset built by many research labs together.

lxc_78b52d45eba5e63a.text: It collected data from 22 different types of robots across 21 institutions, with more than one million robot episodes.

lxc_4b73be5c387fa652.text: The team also trained RT-X models on this shared data.

lxc_3cdb24ae4ea93af8.text: The key idea is that a robot can learn from other robots' experience, not only its own.

lxc_2a37adba2d4d4929.text: OpenVLA is an open-source VLA with about 7 billion parameters.

lxc_92592cd97759357b.text: It was trained on about 970,000 robot episodes from the Open X-Embodiment dataset.

lxc_3b097ceea0fe38a7.text: Anyone can download it and try it on their own robot.

lxc_74b6d2f2fd741a9c.text: In our lens, a VLA does see and act very directly, and the planning is mostly hidden inside the model.

lxc_4c2c8be9de90e7e5.text: Now we come to a different idea.

lxc_5035b84b5572d316.text: JEPA stands for Joint Embedding Predictive Architecture.

lxc_31d023a80297e44d.text: It comes from Yann LeCun, a French-American computer scientist, one of the founders of deep learning, and for many years the chief AI scientist at Meta.

lxc_8ca7501eab317690.text: In 2023, Meta published the first model based on this idea, called I-JEPA, for images.

lxc_15242f25bcaf6b4d.text: Here is the problem JEPA tries to solve.

lxc_84dea4f5add73a5e.text: Many models learn by predicting every pixel of a missing part of an image or the next frame of a video.

lxc_040b54e5289731a6.text: But pixels are full of details that do not matter.

lxc_92ec27f361dfc1ca.text: The exact position of every leaf on a tree is noise, not meaning.

lxc_27ce4e8b210bf748.text: It looks at part of an image, turns it into an abstract representation, and predicts the representation of the missing part.

lxc_5b31cfb931a0b6a4.text: It predicts the meaning of what is missing, not the picture itself.

lxc_a9e60d5217d1adcd.text: This helps learning because the model spends its effort on what matters, like objects and shapes, and ignores tiny details.

lxc_e6d1f37c7f8a7657.text: In our lens, JEPA is mainly about the plan step, learning to predict well.

lxc_afee55c5ed83be93.text: It is a JEPA model for video, and Meta calls it a world model.

lxc_d351444f2835c3c0.text: The idea is the same as before, but now in time.

lxc_c240b2edae2ee3ef.text: The model watches video and learns to predict what comes next in abstract space, not pixel by pixel.

lxc_d62c4e00ae84d550.text: The main model has about 1.2 billion parameters and was trained on more than one million hours of video, with no labels from people.

lxc_52f0e6a008af714f.text: Meta says V-JEPA 2 supports understanding/predicting video, including physical events like how objects move and what people do with them.

lxc_878dfe3844f8dbfc.text: Then comes the robot part, and here we must be careful.

lxc_65dfeaacc67f86dc.text: Meta trained a second version with a small amount of robot data, less than 62 hours.

lxc_4796eb3d893d6a18.text: Meta says this video world model is helping zero-shot robot control in research settings, including cases with little robot data, by using what it learned from ordinary video.

lxc_7e581e1032fead06.text: We should treat that carefully as a research claim, not as a finished home robot.

lxc_0e13b9365589091e.text: In our lens, V-JEPA 2 is strong at the plan step.

lxc_a4ec3c73c68929d4.text: It builds an inner picture of how the world moves, and then robot training can sit on top of that picture.

lxc_49044aad40fea1c3.text: In real labs and factories, robots do not use only one magic model.

lxc_5caa68a2cf6e5158.text: First, classical control is still everywhere.

lxc_24a6076b70218b3c.text: This means clear math and rules for motors, balance, and safe speed.

lxc_4a2816635db02dd7.text: Second, deep learning helps with vision, like finding a cup in a camera picture.

lxc_84b41b5c0046a322.text: Third, Vision-Language-Action models, such as OpenVLA-style systems, help turn a spoken or written goal into actions.

lxc_097be299859dab12.text: Fourth, world-model and JEPA-style ideas are growing.

lxc_5d1bee2271827d97.text: They try to predict what will happen next before the robot moves.

lxc_c7e6609221a9da9f.text: A robot arm must pick up a red block and place it in a box.

lxc_8cd015715f1041f3.text: Classical control keeps the arm smooth and safe.

lxc_a422c33d571417c6.text: A vision model finds the red block in the camera image.

lxc_ffc407b489a4a108.text: A VLA or planner chooses the grasp and the place motion.

lxc_33e04db099afebb8.text: A world model may help the robot imagine the block falling if the gripper is too loose.

lxc_e98d1d5c5675aefe.text: No single system does everything alone.

lxc_adda3b9c7116b72a.text: So the honest picture is this.

lxc_025dc4a57b1111fc.text: Text LLMs are useful for goals and talk.

lxc_0dc7dfcbd7a1b60d.text: Robots still need eyes, hands, timing, and careful engineering.

lxc_1812f443a004a41c.text: VLAs and JEPA-style world models are important new pieces, not the whole machine.
